steps.message:
# Some coins misbehave in the flooded cave

### What happens
`recording.mp4` is an uncut run through a flooded cave basin. Partway through the clip, Tux does something that releases a group of new coins. From that moment until the end of the clip, those coins do not behave the way coins in this game should. The coins that were already placed in the level, Tux, the fish and the scenery in the recording are correct.

### Expected
The released coins should behave like a normal coin burst in this game, from the moment they spread out of the block until they come to rest and Tux collects them. Once a coin is in the water it should drift down slowly. Fix every way the released coins behave wrongly in the recording.

## Attached visual evidence

- `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4` (44 seconds)

You can inspect individual moments of the video by extracting frames from it with `ffmpeg`.

Inspect the attached file before making changes.

steps.message:
I fixed four problems with the coins that come out of a coin-burst block. I couldn't watch the recording first, though: `/app/.harbor_assets/` is empty and `recording.mp4` isn't anywhere on the system. So these fixes come from reading the coin-burst code, not from the video. The build succeeds, but I haven't played the level to confirm the coins now look right.

**1. The burst sprayed half the coins downward and none to the left** (`src/object/coin_explode.cpp`). The left/right sign was applied to the vertical speed instead of the horizontal one. Half the coins shot down into the floor and all of them went right. Now they fan out up and to both sides.

**2. Tux couldn't collect the coins** (`src/object/coin.cpp`, both `HeavyCoin` constructors). The coins were set to collide only with walls and floors, so the game never checked them against Tux. I switched them to the normal moving-object setting. Other code already expects this: trampolines and rocks have checks written for these coins that could never run before.

**3. The coins never came to rest** (`HeavyCoin::collision_solid`). Any landing faster than 20 made a coin bounce again, so in practice they kept bouncing. They also never lost sideways speed, so they slid forever. Now only hard landings (faster than 200) bounce, and a soft landing stops the coin completely.

**4. The coins ignored water** (`HeavyCoin::update`). They now check whether they're in water. If so, gravity drops to 20% and movement slows to 0.4× sideways and 0.6× vertically, so they drift down slowly. These values are copied from how rocks behave in water in this game.

All four changes are in the code shared by every burst coin, so the same coins thrown by an exploding gold bomb get these fixes too. If you can re-attach the recording, I'll check it against these fixes.
